decisions.title: Feet at last
decisions.situation: You pull off one sock. There was a foot in there the whole time. The other sock now looks suspicious.

result.title: Matching feet
result.body: Two socks off. Ten toes accounted for. You start wiggling them.

journal.text: I pulled off both socks and investigated my toes.

decisions.title: Price check on your dignity
decisions.situation: In a quiet shop, you loudly announce that Ava has a bottom. Several shoppers appear to know already.

choices.label: Repeat it for anyone who missed it

result.title: Full coverage
result.body: Ava finishes shopping at record speed.

journal.text: I made a loud announcement about Ava in a shop.

decisions.title: The watermelon investigation
decisions.situation: Ava jokes that swallowing a seed could grow a watermelon in your tummy. You have questions. Several concern the size of your tummy.

choices.label: Demand to know where the leaves go
Draw a plan for your indoor garden
Announce you are growing a fruit salad

result.title: The witness changes their story
result.body: Ava admits it was a joke and explains what seeds actually need. You ask why they left out the soil problem.

journal.text: I questioned Ava until they explained a joke about swallowing seeds.

decisions.title: A very close race
decisions.situation: Your shadow keeps reaching the wall before you. You try standing still. It has apparently thought of that too.

choices.label: Make it do a silly dance

result.title: An obedient rival
result.body: You stop trying to beat the shadow and give it increasingly ridiculous instructions.

journal.text: I made my shadow do a silly dance.

decisions.title: The museum has escaped
decisions.situation: You empty your pocket collection onto the table for Ava. Three stones. A leaf. A slug you thought was another leaf. The slug makes for the edge.

choices.label: Return the slug before it reaches the floor
Claim the slug lives here now

result.title: Please follow the shiny line
result.body: You describe the stones while Ava catches the slug on a leaf. Your only moving exhibit is removed halfway through the tour.

journal.text: I gave Ava a museum tour while a slug escaped from my pocket collection.

decisions.title: Imaginary friend wanted
decisions.situation: Thando is alone at break. They say their imaginary friend has moved to a better school. They are interviewing replacements on the empty part of the bench.

choices.label: Pretend you have accidentally sat on one

result.title: A crowded bench
result.body: You reject the first applicant for imaginary biting. Thando rejects the second for actually being a dragon. You run out of break before making an appointment.

journal.text: I helped Thando interview replacements for an imaginary friend.

decisions.title: The corpse has notes
decisions.situation: During a class play rehearsal, Thando plays the dead monarch. They keep sitting up to complain that your funeral speech is not sad enough. Liam asks you to try once more.

choices.label: Ask the corpse to stop directing
Announce a miracle and cancel the funeral

result.title: A tragic loss to sandwich making
result.body: You praise their kindness, courage and ability to open crisp packets. Thando stays dead for almost the whole speech.

journal.text: I improvised a flattering funeral speech for Thando in a class play.

decisions.title: Apparently this was cool
decisions.situation: Ava plays a song they loved at your age. There is a lengthy explanation of how nobody makes music properly anymore.

choices.label: Ask what it reminds them of

result.title: Before they were your parent
result.body: The story is better than expected. You learn something new about Ava.

journal.text: I listened to Ava’s old music and the story behind it.

decisions.title: Your parent knows this level
decisions.situation: You promise Ava one last round. They sit down, watch your first attempt and say, “I used to beat this blindfolded.” This is an outrageous development.

choices.label: Agree on one round each, then stop

result.title: Dignity preserved
result.body: You keep your promise and turn it off. Ava seems more pleased about that than any old high score.

journal.text: I stopped a game when I had promised Ava I would.

decisions.title: Forwarded with absolutely no evidence
decisions.situation: A group chat is circulating an embarrassing rumour about someone your age. The source appears to be “everyone knows”.

result.title: An inconvenient question
result.body: Nobody produces evidence. The conversation changes topic with suspicious speed.

journal.text: I challenged a rumour in a group chat.

decisions.title: Selective honesty
decisions.situation: Liam has marked a correct answer wrong and a wrong answer right. The mistakes cancel out. You could mention both, or suddenly become very interested in only one.

choices.label: Ask for the lost marks. Hide the free ones.

result.title: No profit, better reputation
result.body: Liam corrects both marks and thanks you for being honest. Your grade stays exactly where it was.

journal.text: I showed Liam two marking mistakes that cancelled each other out.

decisions.title: Sent to the group
decisions.situation: You send “Whoever made this group is unbearable” to the group itself. The admin replies, “Hi.” You can see several people typing.

choices.label: Admit you meant a different chat

result.title: A successful retreat
result.body: You miss the replies and spend the afternoon doing something else. The message remains embarrassing; you stop watching it happen.

journal.text: I muted a group after sending an insulting message to it.

decisions.title: The compliment has the wrong address
decisions.situation: Someone praises an anonymous poem you were standing beside at a free exhibition. You did not write it. They are waiting for you to explain its “raw emotional honesty”.

choices.label: Thank them, then admit it is not yours
Point out the actual poet’s name
Accept the praise and invent your inspiration

result.title: A narrow escape from poetry
result.body: They laugh at the mix-up. You both admit you were not entirely sure what the last line meant.

journal.text: I corrected a stranger who thought I had written a poem.

decisions.title: Everyone here is a winner
decisions.situation: At a motivational taster session, you are asked to name your greatest achievement. The person before you says they survived eight workplace investigations. The facilitator applauds and turns to you.

choices.label: Say you got out of bed today
Ask what the investigations were about

result.title: A standing achievement
result.body: The facilitator calls this a triumph over horizontal thinking. Everyone stands to applaud. You sit down before they can invent a course about it.

journal.text: I told a motivational group that getting out of bed was my achievement.

decisions.title: Water with a personal brand
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, a presenter claims their water has been “emotionally filtered”. The jug beside it is labelled TAP. You are just thirsty.

choices.label: Ask which emotions the filter removes
Debate the emotional lives of liquids

result.title: No emotional processing required
result.body: It tastes like water. The presenter watches you finish a glass with the expression of someone witnessing sabotage.

journal.text: I chose tap water at a premium-water demonstration.

decisions.title: Any difficult questions?
decisions.situation: At a free talk, a speaker claims nobody has ever disproved their theory. The theory is that pigeons remember your face and discuss you at night.

choices.label: Ask how they interviewed the pigeons
Let another questioner take this one
Announce that the pigeons work for you

result.title: The method needs work
result.body: They admit they inferred the conversations. You learn the difference between a suspicious bird and actual evidence.

journal.text: I questioned the evidence behind a speaker’s theory about pigeons.

decisions.title: Your murderous past
decisions.situation: A walking-tour guide points straight at you and tells the group you are the ghost of a notorious murderer. You are outside a shop in Johannesburg, holding a sandwich.

choices.label: Explain that you are alive and eating lunch
Ask what crimes you supposedly committed
Follow the tour without breaking eye contact

result.title: New evidence
result.body: The guide calls your sandwich an unsettling detail. You take a large bite. A tourist asks whether ghosts can eat cheese. The guide moves the group along.

journal.text: I corrected a walking tour that mistook me for a murderer’s ghost in Johannesburg.

decisions.title: Honest feedback, preferably positive
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, you try a cracker that tastes strongly of cupboard. The demonstrator asks for a glowing testimonial while holding a camera.

choices.label: Deliver a dramatic account of the cupboard

result.title: A review they can use
result.body: You mention the texture and the cupboard problem. The camera lowers. They admit this batch has been “challenging”.

journal.text: I gave specific criticism of a free food sample.

decisions.title: You need medical attention

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

journal.text: I helped a film crew recover wind-blown prop money in Johannesburg.

decisions.title: Inner peace is on hold

choices.label: Close your eyes and let them finish
Find peace on a walk outside
Offer to fix the printer problem

result.title: A guided loss of temper
result.body: You breathe slowly through an argument about toner. By the time they hang up, you are considerably calmer than the professional.

journal.text: I relaxed through my relaxation instructor’s furious printer call.

Wear the chicken suit for ZAR 1,485.64
Carry the head around and ask if anyone knows it

result.title: A civilian again
result.body: The volunteer apologises and puts the chicken head on a traffic cone. A child immediately asks the cone for a photo.

journal.text: I declined an emergency shift inside a festival chicken.

result.body: You complete the gentler routine. The instructor says anyone can do it, then folds himself into a shape you decline to investigate.

journal.text: I followed a beginner workout after a fitness video appeared on autoplay.
